title: Amazon Acquires DuckLabs and Integrates DuckDB in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
gist: Amazon acquired DuckLabs, the Amsterdam company behind DuckDB, keeping its founders in charge and the Duck Stack MIT-licensed under the DuckDB Foundation. AWS pitches DuckDB as ideal for the 90%+ of sub-1TB queries and agentic AI exploration, and shipped a first DuckDB-powered Aurora PostgreSQL feature that queries S3/Iceberg data without ETL at no extra charge.

insights.claim: Amazon has acquired DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind the analytical database DuckDB, with co-founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt continuing to lead the team and the project's technical direction inside AWS.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: AWS is buying a popular open-source analytics engine and its founders, strengthening its position in cloud data analytics.
insights.quote: Amazon has announced the acquisition of DuckLabs, the Amsterdam-based company behind the analytical database DuckDB.
insights.locator: Amazon has announced the acquisition of DuckLabs

insights.claim: DuckDB's founders say joining AWS gives them resources and reach to bring DuckDB to many more developers and organizations at a scale they could not reach alone.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Signals that standalone open-source database startups may find hyperscaler distribution more attractive than independent scaling.
insights.quote: Joining AWS gives us the resources and reach to bring this technology to many more developers and organizations
insights.locator: In the announcement on their blog

insights.claim: AWS distinguished engineer Andy Warfield says the AWS-DuckLabs relationship began when the S3 team was building S3 Tables and deepened over roughly two years, including work on AWS Lambda for launching DuckDB queries and DuckDB's ATTACH and CONNECT integrations.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: The deal grew out of long engineering collaboration, suggesting deep integration of DuckDB across AWS data services.
insights.locator: In a piece on Werner Vogels's blog

insights.claim: Warfield frames the acquisition as widening DuckDB's founders' reach so they can set the agenda for how analytics is built and delivered in the cloud, rather than absorbing their work.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: AWS may position DuckDB as a strategic pillar of its cloud analytics offering.
insights.quote: we wanted to give them the broadest possible opportunity to set the agenda not just for DuckDB, but for how analytics should be built and delivered in the cloud
insights.locator: For Warfield, the deal is an

insights.claim: Following Amazon's acquisition of DuckLabs, DuckDB and its 'Duck Stack' components such as DuckLake and Quack will remain free and open-source under the MIT licence, overseen by the non-profit DuckDB Foundation.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Keeps DuckDB available to competing clouds and vendors, limiting AWS lock-in but preserving ecosystem trust.
insights.locator: All the parties involved in the deal

insights.claim: The developer community welcomed the DuckLabs acquisition by Amazon positively but with scepticism, with concerns that it could slow DuckDB's pace of innovation.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Community sentiment is a leading indicator of whether an acquired open-source project keeps momentum.
insights.quote: I hope this doesn't slow the pace of innovation they have been doing
insights.locator: The community has positively welcomed the news

themes.theme: DuckDB's fit for small queries and agentic AI

insights.claim: AWS VP Mai-Lan Tomsen Bukovec says DuckDB targets fast performance for the 90%+ of data queries that run on 1 terabyte of data or less, as in analysis and dashboarding.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: If most queries are small, lightweight engines can displace heavier distributed warehouses for much analytic spend.
insights.quote: DuckDB set out to solve the problem of blazingly fast performance for the 90%+ of data queries in the world today, that often runs 1 terabyte of data or less
insights.locator: In the announcement, Mai-Lan Tomsen Bukovec

insights.claim: According to AWS's Mai-Lan Tomsen Bukovec, AI agents typically inspect data and run small exploratory queries before acting, a pattern that makes DuckDB naturally suited to agentic AI workloads.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Agentic AI could drive demand for fast embedded analytics engines, a rationale for AWS's acquisition.

themes.theme: DuckDB integration in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL

insights.claim: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is the first AWS service to ship a user-facing DuckDB-powered feature, letting a single query combine live operational data with historical data in Apache Iceberg tables via AWS Glue Data Catalog and Parquet/Iceberg data in Amazon S3 and S3 Tables.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Blending transactional and lakehouse analytics inside Aurora could pull workloads away from separate warehouse and ETL vendors.
insights.locator: The integration of DuckDB directly in Aurora PostgreSQL

insights.claim: AWS says the DuckDB integration in Aurora PostgreSQL replaces reverse ETL pipelines that duplicated data between Aurora and Amazon S3, raised infrastructure costs and needed ongoing synchronization effort.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Threatens demand for reverse ETL and data pipeline tooling within the AWS ecosystem.
insights.quote: a common approach was to build reverse ETL pipelines that duplicated data, increased infrastructure costs, and required ongoing engineering effort to keep everything synchronized
insights.locator: Previously, if your application needed to

insights.claim: The DuckDB feature in Aurora PostgreSQL is available in all commercial AWS regions and AWS GovCloud (US) at no additional charge, with customers paying only for incremental Aurora compute and the S3 requests their queries generate.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Free feature monetized via Aurora compute and S3 usage — AWS uses DuckDB to drive consumption of core services.
